title: Eastern Washington University (EWU)
summary: Eastern Washington University (EWU) is a university in Cheney. This entry compiles College Scorecard figures and related sources; UniRepository is not affiliated with EWU.

sections.heading: What EWU is known for
paragraphs: Eastern Washington University (EWU) is a public institution known for its diverse academic offerings and accessible admission policies. With an undergraduate enrollment of 6,222 students, EWU provides a range of programs that cater to various interests and career goals. The university has a notably high admission rate of approximately 90.75%, reflecting its commitment to inclusivity and broad access to higher education.

EWU is recognized for its strong emphasis on business education, with nearly 15% of its programs dedicated to this field. Additionally, health-related programs constitute about 7.7% of the university's academic offerings, highlighting its focus on preparing students for careers in healthcare and related sectors. These program shares illustrate EWU's balanced approach to meeting the educational needs of its student body while supporting regional workforce demands.

sections.heading: How to read EWU tuition
paragraphs: Eastern Washington University (EWU) tuition varies based on residency status. In-state students pay $8,586 annually for tuition, reflecting the lower cost for residents of Washington state. Out-of-state students face a higher tuition rate of $25,959 per year, which accounts for the additional expenses associated with non-resident enrollment. The total cost of attendance at EWU, which includes tuition, fees, room, board, and other expenses, amounts to $24,478. Understanding these figures helps prospective students and families plan for the financial commitment required to attend EWU.

sections.heading: Financial aid
paragraphs: Eastern Washington University (EWU) offers financial aid opportunities to help offset the cost of attendance. Approximately 35.1% of students receive Pell Grants, which are federal subsidies aimed at supporting low-income students. Among those who complete their programs, the median student debt is $19,500, indicating the typical borrowing amount upon graduation. Prospective students can use EWU's net price calculator available at www.ewu.edu to estimate their individual financial aid packages. Additional financial data and resources are accessible through the College Scorecard at https://collegescorecard.ed.gov/school/?235097, providing transparency on costs and aid.
